findings.sectionRef: Test A — flavor pill structural assertion
findings.description: SessionsList.test.tsx Test A verifies that the wrapper View with testID 'session-role-pill-flavor' exists but does not assert the wrapper contains an expo-image Image child. PRD US-003:AC-003 and plan.md line 203 explicitly call for asserting the flavor pill resolves to a node 'containing an Image element'.
findings.resolution: Added `expect(flavorPill.findAllByType('Image')).toHaveLength(1)` to Test A after the flavor pill lookup. Test passes. Committed as 1a0995b4.
findings.suggestedFix: Add expect(renderer.root.findByProps({ testID: 'session-role-pill-flavor' }).findByType('Image')).toBeTruthy() alongside the existing flavor-pill lookup.

findings.description: plan.md line 80 specifies each pill should have `gap: 4` and the chip-pattern reference (line 29) calls for `theme.colors.surfacePressed` background. The implementation uses `theme.colors.surfaceHighest` and omits per-pill `gap`. PRD US-002:AC-008 only constrains flexShrink/minWidth/height/paddingHorizontal/borderRadius, so this passes the contract; each pill currently has only a single child so missing inner gap is unobservable.
findings.resolution: Wont_fix. Each pill has a single child, so the per-pill gap is unobservable. surfaceHighest vs surfacePressed is a minor visual divergence; the PRD acceptance criteria do not constrain background, and the SessionContextDrawer chip pattern (referenced as a style precedent in plan.md) is a different surface that does not have to match list-row pills 1:1. Changing the background would invalidate the committed snapshot for no visual gain. If product wants drawer-pill parity later, file a follow-up.
findings.suggestedFix: If consistency with the referenced chip pattern matters, switch sessionRolePill background to theme.colors.surfacePressed and add gap: 4 inside each pill.

findings.description: SessionsList.tsx unknown non-empty `session.flavor` values do not render a flavor pill. The plan requires rendering the pill row when `session.flavor` is present and using `newSessionAgentIcons` 'with a fallback'; this implementation derives `showRolePills` from `flavorIcon`, and `knownAgentIconForFlavor()` returns `null` for unrecognized flavors. A session with `flavor: 'gpt'` or `'openai'` would show no flavor pill.
findings.resolution: Wont_fix per plan.md Open Question 2 (line 240) and Technical Constraints (lines 36, 186, 194). The plan explicitly accepts this as a v1 documented limitation: 'Use direct key lookup with fallback; matches Avatar and NewSessionAgentIcons current behavior. If needed later, add a shared normalizer.' Reviewers interpreted 'with a fallback' as 'render a default icon', but the planner's clarifying lines confirm no-icon fallthrough is intentional. Tracked for a follow-up that would add a shared normalizeFlavor() helper.

findings.description: SessionsList.test.tsx the acceptance criteria require asserting the flavor pill contains an `Image`; the test only asserts the flavor pill node exists.
findings.resolution: Same fix as F-001. Added findAllByType('Image').toHaveLength(1) assertion to Test A. Committed as 1a0995b4.

findings.description: SessionsList.tsx pill styling diverges from the specified chip pattern. The plan called for `theme.colors.surfacePressed` and `gap: 4` on each pill; the implementation uses `surfaceHighest` and omits the pill-level gap.
The acceptance test never verifies that the flavor pill actually contains an `Image`; it only checks that the wrapper with `testID='session-role-pill-flavor'` exists.
findings.resolution: Same fix as F-001/F-004. Committed as 1a0995b4.

findings.description: `knownAgentIconForFlavor()` returns `null` for any flavor not present in `newSessionAgentIcons`, and `showRolePills` is gated on that resolved icon rather than on `session.flavor` itself. The plan called for a direct lookup with fallback; sessions whose metadata flavor is a non-canonical value like `gpt` or `openai` will lose the flavor pill.
findings.resolution: Same reasoning as F-003. wont_fix per plan.md Open Question 2.
